edges.description: Frameshift and premature stop leave no functional protein product.
TIMMDC1 is required for assembly of the membrane arm and for ND1 module biogenesis; without it the holoenzyme does not mature.
Fewer mature holoenzymes means less NADH:ubiquinone oxidoreductase activity, with complexes II-V unaffected.
Reduced electron entry at complex I lowers ATP output in the tissues least able to tolerate it.

edges.description: The step from chronic ATP deficit to neuronal loss is the least characterised link in this chain and is inherited from the general mitochondrial-disease literature rather than demonstrated for TIMMDC1; typed INDIRECT_UNKNOWN_INTERMEDIATES for that reason.

edges.description: Treating the same fibroblasts with splice-switching oligonucleotides suppresses poison-exon inclusion and restores TIMMDC1 protein, which is the strongest available argument that the intronic variant is the cause rather than a bystander.
edges.limitations: The rescue is in cultured patient fibroblasts over 48 hours. Nothing here addresses delivery to the nervous system, durability, or whether correction after symptom onset would change the clinical course.

nodes.description: Reduced complex I activity lowers mitochondrial ATP output. Patient fibroblasts show low basal oxygen consumption rate, low ATP production and low maximal respiration relative to controls, and these are the measurements that recover when the splicing lesion is corrected - which is what ties the bioenergetic phenotype to TIMMDC1 rather than to anything else in the patient background.

nodes.description:
The clinical syndrome is a mixed central and peripheral neurodegeneration. Reported children have hypotonia and developmental delay with a predominant sensorimotor axonal neuropathy, optic atrophy and cognitive deficit; some show basal ganglia lesions on MRI, and the course is progressive and has been fatal in early childhood in the reported deep-intronic cases.
Marked PROVISIONAL: the clinical picture is well documented but no neuropathological or tissue-level study of TIMMDC1 disease has been published, so the tissue mechanism is assumed from the complex I deficiency rather than observed.

nodes.description: Without TIMMDC1 the ND1 module fails to be built and the subunits that would have joined the holoenzyme are turned over instead. Quantitative proteomics on patient fibroblasts shows reduced ND1 together with reduced ND1-module subunits NDUFA8 and NDUFA13 and other complex I subunits, and the discovery cohort found globally decreased complex I subunit levels by both proteomics and western blot. The loss is of assembled complex rather than of transcription: the subunit genes are intact and the defect is post-translational.

nodes.description:
The biochemical signature is an isolated complex I defect: where skeletal muscle respiratory chain enzymology was performed in reported patients it confirmed complex I deficiency with the other complexes spared, and the discovery cohort found the same isolated pattern in muscle.
This node carries the entry's most clinically consequential negative claim. Plasma lactate was not raised and routine metabolic investigation was unremarkable in the reported cases, so the deficiency is invisible to the screening tests that normally raise suspicion of mitochondrial disease. A normal lactate does not exclude this diagnosis.

nodes.description:
TIMMDC1 is a multi-pass inner mitochondrial membrane protein that acts as an assembly factor for complex I, and in particular for the biogenesis of the mitochondrially encoded core subunit ND1. Patient cells carrying the poison-exon allele have almost no detectable TIMMDC1 protein; in the discovery cohort the protein could not be detected at all by quantitative proteomics.
The node is kept separate from the splicing node because it is the level at which the rescue experiments read out: restoring the protein is what the antisense oligonucleotides achieve, and what everything downstream is then measured against.

nodes.description:
Two splice-switching oligonucleotides, SSO1 and SSO2, target the region around the pathogenic intronic enhancer and suppress inclusion of the poison exon. In patient fibroblasts they restore normal TIMMDC1 message, restore protein to at least parental levels, restore complex I subunit abundance by quantitative proteomics, and raise oxygen consumption, ATP production and maximal respiration. A non-targeting control oligonucleotide does none of this.
This is preclinical. It has been shown only in cultured patient fibroblasts, there is no animal work and no trial, and the approach would be allele-specific - it treats the splicing lesion, so it has nothing to offer a patient whose alleles are both nonsense variants. It is curated because the mechanism makes it the one plausible disease-modifying route in a disease that otherwise has none.
On the structured detail below: the oligonucleotide suppresses inclusion of an aberrant pseudoexon rather than skipping a constitutive exon, and SPLICE_MODULATION_EXON_SKIPPING is the closest available enum value. Chemistry and conjugation are not stated in the source and are left absent rather than guessed.

nodes.description:
The recurrent pathogenic allele is not a coding change. c.597-1340A>G (equivalently c.596+2146A>G under the earlier transcript numbering) lies deep within intron 5 and acts as a splicing enhancer, causing an ~80 bp cryptic exon to be spliced into the mature transcript between exons 5 and 6. The inserted exon shifts the reading frame and introduces a premature termination codon (p.Gly199_Thr200ins5*), so the aberrant message is degraded by nonsense-mediated decay.
Curated as the trigger node rather than as a variant annotation because the splicing event is the mechanism: everything downstream follows from the transcript, and the one available therapeutic handle acts here and nowhere else.

nodes.description: Dermal fibroblasts from the two affected homozygous siblings, with heterozygous parental and unrelated healthy-control fibroblasts as comparators. Because the lesion is a splicing defect in a ubiquitously expressed gene, fibroblasts carry the full molecular phenotype - poison-exon transcript, absent protein, reduced complex I subunits and reduced respiration - which is why a skin biopsy substitutes for inaccessible neural tissue here.
